message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong that I didn't read a book to my son tonight because he has to go to school tomorrow. Let me break this down step by step. First, I know that reading to my son is something we usually do before bed. It's a routine we've established, and I think it's important for his development. Reading helps with his vocabulary, imagination, and it's a bonding time for us. So, not doing it tonight might disrupt that routine. But why didn't I read to him tonight? Because he has school tomorrow. Maybe I thought he needed to go to bed earlier to get enough rest. That makes sense because school days require him to be well-rested. If he's tired, he might not perform as well or might be cranky. On the other hand, skipping the reading might make him feel like the routine is broken. He might feel upset or miss that special time with me. It could also affect his sleep if he's expecting the usual wind-down activity. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could have read a shorter book or just a few pages to maintain the routine without taking too much time. That way, he still gets the benefits of reading and the routine isn't completely broken. Another thought: perhaps the reason for not reading was more about time management. Maybe I had other things to do, or I was tired. But as a parent, I should prioritize his well-being and routine, even if it means adjusting my own schedule. I also think about the importance of consistency in routines for children. Consistent bedtime routines help with sleep patterns and overall behavior. So, skipping part of the routine might have unintended consequences. In conclusion, while the intention to ensure he gets enough rest is good, not reading to him might have negative effects on his routine and emotional well-being. It might be better to find a way to include reading, even if it's a shorter session, to maintain the routine.
